preamble: Monophthongization of the diphthong /ai/ to the open-mid front vowel /ɛ/ (often long [ɛː]) fuses the open onset and the high offglide into a single mid vowel. It happened independently in Late Latin (ae > [ɛː], the source of Romance open e), in Koine Greek (αι > /ɛ(ː)/, later /e/), and in Old French (⟨ai⟩ /aj/ > /ɛ/ after the mid-12th century).

examples.note: Classical /ae̯/ monophthongized to [ɛː] by around the 2nd century AD and merged with the reflex of short ĕ, hence Italian open [ɛ] in cielo.
Boeotian wrote η for αι already in the early 4th century BC; confusion of αι with ε in Egyptian papyri by about 150 BC shows Koine /ɛ(ː)/, later /e/ (Modern Greek και [ce]).
In Early Old French (to about the mid-12th century) ⟨ai⟩ spelled the diphthong /aj/; it then became the monophthong /ɛ/, which the spelling still records (lait, faire, mais).

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2025). Old French: Phonology. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_French
